initialNumericalReport.program: Sexual assault counseling, advocacy and prevention education

what: ZCenter provides free, confidential support to sexual assault survivors and their families in Lake and northern Cook counties.
Its services include counseling in English and Spanish, a support line and referrals.
Advocacy and prevention education complement counseling at its Gurnee location, while Skokie currently provides counseling only.
strengths: Free bilingual services reduce barriers to specialist support.
Individual and group counseling offer a plausible route to short-term trauma recovery.
Local referrals and advocacy can help survivors navigate additional needs.
reservations: Local completion and incremental clinical outcomes were not verified.
External adult therapy evidence does not establish durable benefits or child outcomes.
Net household resources, access burdens and marginal donor response remain uncertain.

sections.what: Zacharias Sexual Abuse Center, EIN 36-3314976, provides free individual and group counseling to adults and children, a confidential English/Spanish support line and referrals. Gurnee in Lake County also provides advocacy and outreach; Skokie in Cook County currently provides counseling only. Both locations fall within the Chicago metro boundary. The official giving page identifies the independent recipient, but no donation transaction was tested. [Services](https://zcenter.org/survivor-services/services/)
sections.monitoring: Track unique adult counseling participants, treatment completion, validated PTSD and depression measures, adverse effects, actual alternative services, time and transport burdens and collected net household resources. Intake contact within 24–48 business hours is not completed care. Prevention reach, calls and group attendances are not interchangeable with unique people or clinical benefit. Children's services, prevention education, family support and advocacy are real activities but remain unpriced in this limited adult reference.
sections.qualitative: Cochrane's 2023 review of 36 randomized studies found possible short-term PTSD and depression improvement after psychosocial interventions for adult survivors. It rates the symptom evidence low certainty, reports substantial heterogeneity and missing outcomes, and does not establish durable benefit. Adverse events were poorly monitored. The review searched through January 2022 and predominantly studied adult women; it is not a child-specific coefficient or a ZCenter evaluation. The .03 incremental utility and six-month duration below are judgments, not a conversion of standardized symptom scores into observed QALYs. Existing free community and public services remain in the counterfactual.
sections.cost:
FY2025 original recognized expense is $2,454,250 plus $61,260 direct fundraising expense netted from revenue: $2,515,510 gross recognized annual recipient cost. No rental expense group was identified. The annual whole-recipient denominator includes education, advocacy, administration and nonclinical work, while the numerator prices only a conditional adult counseling/access channel. It is not a verified marginal expansion price.

A judged 300 local adult household opportunities, .5 additional annual-work response and .6 completion imply 150 exposed households and 90 clinical participants. One clinical person and one welfareperson are modeled per household; other family welfare remains unpriced. The clinical cohort is a subset of resource exposure, so full union harms and resource burdens include all 150 even if clinical benefit fails. Incremental .03 utility for half a year, after a quarter-year delay at 3%, gives 1.340061 clinical QALYs. PTSD and depression are not separately stacked.

A separate conditional .2 additional resource success among all 150 exposed households gives 30 changed households. A judged $1,500 net gain from successful access/referrals or protected work resources retains .5 for health overlap, then full $100 attendance/time/transport burden leaves $650. The other 120 households lose $100. At $30,000 annual household resources, one finite year gives .5 × [30 log(1 + 650/30,000) + 120 log(1 − 100/30,000)] / 1.03^.25 = .120303 equivalent healthy years. Combined 1.460364 implies $17.225232 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

No retail counseling fee, gross salary or ordinary survivor earnings is counted as income. Resource gain is after taxes, benefit withdrawal, replacement earnings and new access or work costs; separate attendance costs cover therapy participation, travel and care arrangements. Resource success does not require clinical efficacy. Positive benefits alone receive overlap adjustment; negative effects and costs remain full before one joint household log. The central counterparty and outside care ledger is unknown-neutral, not observed zero. Matched payer losses, external care costs, negative resources and adverse utility are explicit stresses. Complete portfolio, nonlocal incidence and public opportunity costs remain unknown.
sections.funding: FY2025 government grants are $1,236,493 and net assets $7,241,412. FY2024 expense $2,065,387 plus $85,671 event cost totals $2,151,058; FY2023 $1,856,596 plus $37,680 totals $1,894,276. Three comparable July–June annual gross recognized totals average $2,186,948. The official appeal supports free services across the organization. Government replacement and a specific unfunded capacity tranche were not established; neither large reserves nor government grants alone proves a donor bottleneck. The .5 response is a conditional annual funded-work comparison against alternatives, with b=1 separately shown. [Original latest return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631359349307348/IRS990)

model.geographicAttribution: Lake and Cook county adult counseling household opportunities; all modeled local. Other programs unpriced.
model.formula: Q=(positiveOnly(N*b*completion*q*T,clinicalOverlap)−N*b*harm)/(1+d)^delay. Household gain=positiveOnly(gain,positiveOverlap)−full attendance cost; changes jointly net before .5*people*log(1+gain/baseline), one finite year. Price=10*C/(health+resources).
model.counterfactual: Alternative free specialist, community and public services continue; resource gains are additionally collected net resources, not avoided retail fees.
model.attribution: Completion, additional annual response, incremental utility and resource success are distinct conditional judgments.
model.uncertainty: Adult short-term therapy mechanism supported; recipient-specific utility, duration, net resources, complete portfolio and marginal donor conversion unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Unique adult treatment completion, finite incremental trauma utility, signed collected net household resources, attendance and counterparty burdens.
